title: ATOMS: ALMA three-millimetre observations of massive star-forming regions - XIV. Properties of resolved ultra-compact H II regions
question: What are the physical properties (electron density, emission measure, electron temperature, ionic abundance ratio n_He+/n_H+, and line widths) and internal spatial variations of resolved ultra-compact H II regions in the ATOMS survey?

recipe.goal: Identify UC HII regions and measure effective radii and spectral parameters
recipe.method: Integrate H40alpha and He40alpha cubes along the velocity axis to produce intensity maps, visually identify compact UC HII regions, compute effective radius R_eff = sqrt(S/pi) from the area S within 5-sigma contours, and fit Gaussians to source-averaged spectra to obtain peak intensity, v_lsr, and line width Delta_V.
key_parameters: 5-sigma contour threshold for area S; neglect unresolved regions smaller than one beam
assumptions: 3 mm continuum emission is dominated by free-free emission

recipe.goal: Derive emission measure and electron density from H40alpha emission
recipe.method: Compute H40alpha line luminosity from integrated line flux and distance, then calculate electron density n_e (Eq. 2) and emission measure EM (Eq. 4) using R_eff.
key_parameters: Recombination efficiency eta = 1.99e-32 at T_e = 10^4 K and n_e = 10^4 cm^-3
assumptions: Case B recombination; helium ionization and stimulated emission negligible; homogeneous medium of thickness 2 R_eff

recipe.goal: Measure ionic abundance ratio Y+ = n_He+/n_H+ and its spatial variation
recipe.method: Calculate Y+ as the ratio of integrated intensities of He40alpha to H40alpha (Eq. 5) both source-averaged and pixel-by-pixel, and compare Y+ across contour intervals (80%, 60%, 40%, 30%, 20% of peak H40alpha emission).
key_parameters: Contour levels at 80%, 60%, 40%, 30%, 20% of peak H40alpha emission
assumptions: Both helium and hydrogen RRLs are in LTE

recipe.goal: Derive non-LTE electron temperature and 3 mm continuum electron density
recipe.method: Model continuum and H40alpha line intensities using non-LTE departure coefficients and radiative transfer (Appendix A), fit T_e and n_e to random realizations drawn from measured intensities via least-squares, and compute 3 mm continuum EM and n_e (Appendix B).
assumptions: 3 mm continuum is purely free-free emission; Rayleigh-Jeans approximation; homogeneous medium of thickness D = 2R; no strong RRL maser

recipe.goal: Decompose H40alpha line broadening and test Galactic T_e gradient
recipe.method: Calculate thermal and pressure broadening following Peters et al. (2012), derive microturbulent broadening Delta_V_tur = sqrt(Delta_V^2 - Delta_V_th^2), and perform linear regression of T_e against galactocentric distance R_GC.
assumptions: Pressure broadening is negligible for n_e between 10^3 and 10^5 cm^-3 at H40alpha

Code or lookup tables for the non-LTE departure coefficients b_k from Zhu et al. (2019, 2022) used in Appendix A

score_reason: Public ALMA dataset (2019.1.00685.S), explicit analytical equations in the text and appendices, and full measurement tables (Tables 1 and C1) for all 94 regions, but imaging details and source distances are deferred to companion papers and the non-LTE departure coefficient code is not released.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA data are public, all 94 UC HII regions have tabulated observables and derived physical parameters (R_eff, EM, n_e, Y+, T_e, Delta_V), and the analytical/non-LTE formulas linking the observables to the physical quantities are explicitly provided.
